description: The European Marine Casualty Information Platform (EMCIP) is the database and data distribution system for marine casualties and incidents operated by the European Maritime Safety Agency with the European Commission and the EU and EEA member states, operational since June 2011, when notification and reporting of safety investigation data became mandatory under Directive 2009/18/EC. Coverage: casualties and incidents involving all types of ships, including occupational accidents in ship operations, on EU-flagged ships, in member states' territorial seas and internal waters, or wherever member state interests are involved, as reported by the accident investigation bodies of the member states, Iceland and Norway; the data grow by about 4,000 incidents a year, and EMCIP links to the IMO's Global Integrated Shipping Information System. The public side comprises investigation reports, anonymised casualty data and EMSA's Annual Overview of Marine Casualties and Incidents, published since 2014 (editions for 2022 to 2025 on the publications page, last updated 29 May 2026), which present casualty statistics, plus safety analyses such as one of navigation accidents. Format and access: annual overviews as PDF (full and lite versions); the EMCIP database itself is for member state authorities; free. Licence: EMSA copyright and disclaimer; no open licence stated. Caveats: the statistics carry no warranty of accuracy or completeness; the public anonymised data access point was not read. Simulation uses: incident frequencies and causes for port and shipping lane risk, maritime emergency response planning and resilience studies. Related records: Norway's open AIS feed (data-kystverket-open-real-time-ais-norway) gives the traffic exposure against which casualty rates can be set.
